references.text: Joshua 9 describes how the Gibeonites became woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation of Israel, corresponding to the description of the lowest services mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:10.
Joshua cursed the Gibeonites to be woodcutters and water carriers, the same tasks mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:10.
The same inclusion of the entire people—men, women, children, and foreigners—in the covenant assembly.
Reference to the foreigner (ger) living among the Israelites, also mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:10.
Describes the mixture of people who left Egypt together with the Israelites, including foreigners who later became part of the community.
The law applies both to the native Israelite and to the foreigner living among them.
The foreigner within the gates is mentioned in the Sabbath commandment, showing the inclusion of foreigners in Israel's religious life.
